assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates as liquid-liquid phase-separated compartments established a new physical-chemical principle of cellular organisation: thermodynamic demixing driven by multivalent, weak interactions, with phase diagrams, saturation concentrations and material properties describing intracellular structure. It reaches from membraneless organelles to disease-linked aggregation, and speaks directly to my own field of self-assembly and phase behaviour.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne demonstrated liquid-like P granules and the condensate concept in cells; Rosen showed that multivalent interacting modules reconstitute phase separation in vitro. Pappu and Mittag made important sequence-encoded theory and biophysics contributions but a three-person prize is most defensible with the first demonstrations of the concept.
assessment.maturity: Concept is widely adopted and independently reproduced, but the field is still debating how general physiological phase separation is versus other assemblies, and some in-cell claims have been challenged. Timely, though a few more years of consolidation would not hurt.
uncertainties: Extent to which in-cell condensates are true equilibrium phase-separated liquids is debated.
Credit between Hyman/Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is not fully settled; I rely on memory for the early history and have not verified it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a clear case of lipid self-assembly and physical chemistry turned into a medicine: pH-dependent charge control of lipid packing and encapsulation enabled siRNA and mRNA delivery, with enormous demonstrated impact through COVID-19 vaccines. This is a field where membrane and phase behaviour knowledge was decisive.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues (Hope, Madden) developed lipid-based nucleic-acid encapsulation and the ionizable lipid concept; MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer contributed formulations and lipid optimisation. Attribution is crowded and partly overlaps with 2023 Medicine recognition of mRNA modification, so the chemistry prize must be framed around the lipid delivery vehicle.
assessment.maturity: Clinical and commercial validation is exceptional and independent, so recognition is timely and mature.
uncertainties: Selecting three among a larger credited group is contentious.
Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize and whether the Chemistry committee sees this as chemistry or pharmaceutics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy-landscape and funnel picture resolved Levinthal's paradox and recast protein folding as statistical mechanics of a minimally frustrated landscape. It is a general physical-chemical principle with very strong conceptual originality, and it is complemented by experimental mapping of folding transition states and pathways.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic are central to the funnel and frustration theory, Fersht to the experimental phi-value analysis and kinetics. Bryngelson and Dill are also decisive early contributors, so any trio leaves out important credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature, decades of confirmation; AlphaFold's 2024 prize addressed structure prediction rather than folding mechanism, so this is complementary rather than superseded, although some may regard the folding problem as partly recognised.
uncertainties: Possible perception that 2024 Chemistry already covered protein folding.
Allocation among Wolynes, Onuchic, Dill, Bryngelson and Fersht is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled monolayers and soft lithography created a general way to control surface chemistry at the molecular level, grounded in interfacial thermodynamics and molecular organisation. They shaped surface science, microfluidics, biointerfaces and nanofabrication, and fit the kind of molecular-organisation concept I value.
assessment.attribution: Nuzzo and Allara reported thiol/gold SAMs with Whitesides' extensive subsequent development and soft lithography; Sagiv's earlier silane monolayers complicate priority, and Xia is credited for soft-lithography extensions.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and widely used, perhaps late rather than premature; the breadth of the field makes a single focused citation harder.
uncertainties: Priority between Sagiv, Nuzzo/Allara and Whitesides is disputed.
Whether the prize would focus on SAMs or soft lithography is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Two-dimensional infrared spectroscopy opened ultrafast structural dynamics of molecules and biomolecules, including hydrogen-bond dynamics in water, peptide and amyloid structure, and membrane-associated systems. It is a significant physical-chemical method that is relevant to my own interest in aggregation structure.
assessment.attribution: The method was developed by several groups; Hamm, Zanni and Tokmakoff are important experimental pioneers and authors of the field's applications, while Mukamel (theory) and Fleming (nonlinear optical lineage) are also credited. The late Hochstrasser's role is not in the supplied credit, which complicates a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Method is well established and independently reproduced, but wide-reaching adoption beyond specialist labs is more limited than for other methods.
uncertainties: Method-development prizes require clear dominant originators, which is unclear here.
I am relying on memory for the priority history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers produced a spectacular rise in solar-cell efficiency within a decade and a new materials family with striking defect tolerance, with an important chemistry of composition, crystallisation and stability.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cell, Park and Snaith the solid-state efficiency leap, with Seok, Grätzel and Kanatzidis also major contributors. Credit is contested among many.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency record is very strong but long-term stability and commercialisation are not settled, so recognition could be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Device stability and scalability remain unresolved.
Allocation among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Seok, Grätzel is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation through PROTACs and molecular glues introduced a new modality that hijacks the ubiquitin system by induced proximity, with a strong molecular-recognition chemistry component and a growing clinical pipeline.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept; Ciulli contributed structure-guided VHL-based degraders. Molecular glue discoveries (Handa, Ito, Gray, and others) are a separate part of the compound candidate that may need different recognition.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is still emerging, so it may be somewhat premature, although concept confirmation is broad.
uncertainties: Compound candidate combining PROTACs and glue degraders makes laureate selection difficult.
Clinical outcome evidence is still maturing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic-code expansion with orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs allowed site-specific incorporation of noncanonical amino acids in living cells, a major chemical-biology invention with wide use in protein engineering and mechanism studies.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang reported the first in vivo expansion in E. coli and yeast; Chin extended it to higher organisms and quadruplet/ribosome engineering. Mehl and Yokoyama made significant contributions to orthogonal pairs and structural design.
assessment.maturity: Technology is mature and independently reproduced, though broad impact is mainly as an enabling tool.
uncertainties: The relative weight of Schultz, Chin and Wang is uncertain.
Whether the committee views it as sufficient breadth of impact.
